title: A worker-controlled route through automation-related work change
hypothesis_summary: A reversible support rehearsal may help affected workers preserve meaningful choice while institutions learn where access, refusal, review and communication safeguards fail.

outcome_scope.who: Affected workers inside the complete registered observation scope
outcome_scope.standard: without involuntary loss of real earnings or essential conditions, while retaining a credible alternative and accessible human review

competing_paths.label: Work is redesigned in place with protected roles
competing_paths.selection_reason: It could preserve the chosen outcome without occupational transition support as the main mechanism.
competing_paths.incompatible_claim: Most adaptation occurs inside retained roles rather than through the candidate support route.

discriminating_observations.construct: Worker-level role retention, task redesign and use of transition support
discriminating_observations.possible_path_pattern: Affected workers voluntarily use a credible option and accessible review route.
discriminating_observations.competing_path_pattern: Affected workers retain redesigned roles and rarely use transition support.
discriminating_observations.source_plan: Pre-register consented worker observations and independently audited employer task records. No source is acquired here.

competing_paths.label: Work contracts without a protected route
competing_paths.selection_reason: It tests whether apparent adaptation hides exits, lost earnings or constrained choice.
competing_paths.incompatible_claim: Affected workers leave or lose work without the registered option and review safeguards.

discriminating_observations.construct: Worker exits, real earnings, essential conditions and registered support exposure
discriminating_observations.possible_path_pattern: Affected workers retain the chosen standard with a recorded credible option and review route.
discriminating_observations.competing_path_pattern: Affected workers exit without the safeguards or do not retain the chosen standard.
discriminating_observations.source_plan: Acquire consented longitudinal worker records with independent access and harm audits. No source is acquired here.

roles.unresolved_reason: The chosen human outcome has no independently validated measure.
The proposed rehearsal has not started and no governed exposure record exists.

affected_populations.label: General Clerks and Payroll Clerks in the registered New South Wales scope
affected_populations.effect_channel: Work, real earnings, essential conditions, choice, review access and information harm

affected_populations.label: Households that depend on earnings from affected workers
affected_populations.effect_channel: Income stability, care responsibilities and mobility burden

entries.label: Workers with temporary, visa-linked, casual or otherwise precarious bargaining positions
entries.omission_reason: The registered aggregate scope does not separately represent constraints on refusal, appeal or mobility.
entries.consequence: A route described as voluntary for the aggregate may remain coercive for these workers.
entries.remedy: Co-design separate refusal, continuity and review tests with affected workers and qualified advocates before use.
entries.public_notice: Workers with precarious bargaining positions are not adequately represented by this synthetic path.

omissions.search_method: Synthetic enumeration across worker, household, employer, service, legal-status and communication channels.
omissions.search_limitations: No affected-party consultation or representative sampling has occurred. Further omissions are expected.

gaming_and_reflexivity.mechanism: A provider or employer could relabel constrained redeployment as a credible option.
gaming_and_reflexivity.early_observation: Audit refusal, appeal use, adverse employment events and worker comprehension before interpreting coverage.
gaming_and_reflexivity.response: Pause the path, retain records and require worker-accessible independent review.
gaming_and_reflexivity.residual_unknown: Informal coercion may remain hidden even when formal refusal is recorded.

gaming_and_reflexivity.mechanism: Publishing a favourable rule state could be mistaken for empirical truth, entitlement or permission.
gaming_and_reflexivity.early_observation: Test whether affected people can distinguish rule state, evidence quality, freshness and authority.
gaming_and_reflexivity.response: Withdraw or redesign communication when misunderstanding or pressure rises.
gaming_and_reflexivity.residual_unknown: Public interpretation may change as institutions respond to the signal.

expiry.reason: Evidence, definitions, worker preferences and institutional capability may change.

triggers.condition: The exact IF receipt is false, unknown, stale, conflicted or mechanically invalid.
triggers.reason: No consequential route may inherit assurance from missing, old or disputed evidence.

triggers.condition: An affected or omitted population reports material harm that the registered scope does not cover.
triggers.reason: Aggregate progress cannot silently trade away an under-represented population.

abandonment.public_notice: Stopping this candidate path does not establish a competitor. It records what failed and what must be learned next.

governance.authority_next_check: Name and independently verify a lawful owner with affected-party challenge before any decision-linked use.

public_claim_ceiling: Synthetic possible path, not a finding: Affected workers inside the complete registered observation scope may navigate automation-related work change to the following standard: without involuntary loss of real earnings or essential conditions, while retaining a credible alternative and accessible human review, in New South Wales, Australia, during 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z, only if Affected workers in the registered scope retain a credible alternative and an accessible human review route, at the standard that both registered protection predicates are satisfied, from 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z through 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z. Affected populations: General Clerks and Payroll Clerks in the registered New South Wales scope; Households that depend on earnings from affected workers. Scope omissions: Workers with precarious bargaining positions are not adequately represented by this synthetic path. Named competing paths: Work is redesigned in place with protected roles; Work contracts without a protected route. This open-world hypothesis is unscored and grants no action authority.
